title: Market Requirements for a federated research and creation estate: a typed relational ontology with explicit provenance classification
description:
This record documents the requirements of a federated estate of independently existing research and creation systems, expressed not as a product catalogue but as a typed relational ontology accompanied by a registry and a constitutional map. Components are described as sovereign systems that own their ontology, runtime, artifacts, evolution and users; interoperability between them is represented through typed edges rather than containment, so that a system participating in a shared environment is not thereby made a module of it.

The distinguishing feature is the treatment of provenance within the document itself. Every entity carries one of four classifications: corroborated in a durable record or live repository; named but incompletely recorded; present only in a prior synthesis produced by an assistant, which is explicitly marked as not constituting evidence; or unresolved, where the record does not contain the information and no substitute has been supplied. This responds to an identified failure mode in which a reconstruction becomes a document, the document is later consulted as a source, and a further reconstruction is built upon it, producing a chain of assertions with no external anchor.

The material comprises a constitutional layer distinguishing registry, provenance and evidence as separate concerns; lineage descriptions that preserve parallel branches rather than collapsing them into single genealogies; a component register with problem statements, scope including explicit refusals, ontological primitives with their forbidden substitutions, numbered requirements, invariants, observed failure modes, evidence requirements and open questions; and a statement of items deliberately left unresolved.

Both documents are generated from the accompanying machine-readable data rather than maintained by hand.
